title: wicked conformance-rules (v1.1.0)
description: PRESCRIPTIVE sibling of the descriptive domain-model — the store of architecture/design PATTERN rules and compliance/security POLICY rules that agent outputs are checked AGAINST (garden STEERS, crew GOVERNS, wicked-testing ASSERTS). Where domain-model facts are MINED FROM code (descriptive), conformance rules are AUTHORED/INGESTED and applied TO code (prescriptive). It rides the SAME spine as @wicked/domain-model-schema: every rule carries a numeric `confidence` in [0,1] AND a `provenance{source, ref, source_kinds}` (identical $def to domain-model), and a rule may bind to code via an OPTIONAL estate `symbol_ref` SymbolId REFERENCE — never a copy of the symbol's code/name/file/line (contract invariant #5). TWO rule_types: `pattern` (architecture/design, e.g. 'the repository layer must not import the web layer') and `policy` (compliance/security, e.g. 'no secret literals in source'). `severity` (info|warn|error|critical) advises the downstream enforcer how hard to fail; the store does NOT enforce — enforcement + any conform/violate verdict is a garden/crew/wicked-testing concern, so a rule carries NO coverage field (coverage in the descriptive world means 'every behavior-bearing SymbolId is accounted for'; the prescriptive analogue — does code CONFORM — is an enforcement-time result owned downstream, not a property of the rule). HARD INVARIANTS mirrored from the donor: `metadata.schema_version` is REQUIRED + `const` '1.0.0' — a consumer REJECTS a schema_version it has no validator for (no silent best-effort); `confidence` is a REQUIRED number in [0,1] (a confidence-less or non-numeric-confidence rule is a hard validation failure, not a warning — here confidence measures INGEST FIDELITY: how sure we are this is a real, correctly-transcribed rule from its source, since a doc-only source rests on source_kinds:['doc'] and is trust-eligible only, not proven); `additionalProperties:false` EVERYWHERE. The `id`/`rule_type` coupling (PAT-* => pattern, POL-* => policy) is enforced WRITE-TIME by conformance-store's enforceConformanceInvariants (INV-C1), not by the schema — the bundle's hand-rolled draft-07 validator supports a single if/then per object but no else/allOf, so a bidirectional two-branch coupling lives in the store exactly as domain-store's INV-1/2/3 do. v1.1.0 (STEERING): the standalone governance Policy model MERGED into this rule model — a rule may now carry steering_type (one of seven steering pages), applies_to/excludes phase scoping, an ordering/priority weight, and the optional enforcement half (effect/trigger/obligations/criteria; a rule WITHOUT effect is recall-only exactly as v1.0.0). All new fields are OPTIONAL with defaulted read-back (steering_type=architecture, weight=1.0), so every 1.0.0 document remains valid; the id pattern is relaxed because migrated policies keep their original (non PAT-/POL-) ids — the PAT-/POL- shape stays enforced write-time (INV-C1) within that reserved namespace.

provenance.description: Where a rule came from and how it is grounded. IDENTICAL shape to @wicked/domain-model-schema domain-model.schema.json#/$defs/provenance — the shared spine, not a parallel representation. A conformance rule ingested from a wiki/doc carries source_kinds:['doc'] (trust-eligible only, per the spine's TRUST RULE); a rule hand-verified against code may carry ['code-body'] / ['type-def'].

source.description: The origin unit the rule came from — repo / service / wiki space / doc set.

ref.description: The specific reference within the source — file#anchor, wiki page id, or an estate SymbolId. A REFERENCE, never a copy of the symbol's structure.

source_kinds.description: The grounding tier: code-body = executable logic read directly; type-def = type/schema/interface declaration; comment = inline prose; doc = README/wiki/external. TRUST RULE (shared with domain-model): a rule is 'trusted' only when grounded in code-body and/or type-def; resting on comment/doc alone makes it trust-eligible, not proven.

targets.description: Targeting facets that scope WHERE a rule applies — the recall query keys. Every facet is OPTIONAL; an ABSENT facet is a WILDCARD (the rule applies to all values of that facet). conformance-store's recall API matches a rule when, for each queried facet, the rule's facet is absent (applies broadly) OR equals the query value.

language.description: Programming language the rule scopes to (e.g. 'python', 'rust', 'typescript'). Absent = all languages.

layer.description: Architectural layer the rule scopes to (e.g. 'repository', 'domain', 'web', 'service'). Absent = all layers.

framework.description: Framework the rule scopes to (e.g. 'express', 'django', 'axum'). Absent = all frameworks.

rule.description: A single prescriptive conformance rule. HARD INVARIANT: confidence is a REQUIRED number in [0,1] and provenance is REQUIRED — a confidence-less, non-numeric-confidence, or provenance-less rule is a hard validation failure, not a warning (mirrors domain-model's rule $def). The id/rule_type coupling (PAT-* => pattern, POL-* => policy) is enforced write-time by the store (INV-C1), not here.

id.description: Stable rule id, unique within rules[]. The `PAT-`/`POL-` prefix is the RESERVED doc-ingest namespace: an id in it must match ^(PAT|POL)-[0-9]{3,6}$ with the prefix agreeing with rule_type (enforced write-time, INV-C1). Ids outside that namespace (policies migrated into steering rules keep their original ids; UI/chat-authored steering rules mint their own) need only be non-blank.

rule_type.description: pattern = architecture/design rule (structural: what may/may not depend on what, layering, boundaries). policy = compliance/security rule (safety: secrets, authn, PII, licensing). The distinction is advisory metadata for routing to the right enforcer, not a shape difference — both variants share the identical field set.

statement.description: The prescriptive rule text — an imperative the enforcer checks agent output against (e.g. 'The repository layer must not import the web layer').

severity.description: How hard a violation should fail downstream. ADVISORY: the store persists it; the enforcer (garden/crew) and the QE gate (wicked-testing) decide the mapping (e.g. error/critical => block a gate; info/warn => annotate). The store does NOT gate on severity.

symbol_ref.description: OPTIONAL estate SymbolId this rule binds to — a REFERENCE, never a copy of the symbol's code/name/file/line (contract invariant #5, same as domain facts). estate GROUNDS the symbol; brain owns the rule content. Absent when the rule is a free-standing architectural/policy constraint not yet bound to a specific symbol.

compliance.description: OPTIONAL binding of a (typically policy) rule to an external compliance framework's control (e.g. framework 'soc2', control_id 'CC6.1'). RESOLVED/EXECUTED at load time by a pluggable ComplianceFramework (conformance-frameworks.mjs): the shipped default is a config-driven NO-OP that accepts any framework/control, and real frameworks (SOC2/PCI/HIPAA) drop in behind the same interface — so the store + downstream enforcement test the SEAM once, not each framework.

framework.description: Compliance framework name resolved by the framework registry (e.g. 'soc2', 'pci-dss'). Distinct from targets.framework (the CODE framework like 'express'). The no-op default accepts any name.

control_id.description: The specific control within the framework (e.g. 'CC6.1', '6.5.1') a violation traces to.

confidence.description: REQUIRED numeric ingest-fidelity confidence in [0,1] — how sure we are this is a real, correctly-transcribed rule from its source. Not fabricated: a doc-ingested rule defaults conservatively; a human-ratified rule is higher. Non-numeric/absent is a hard validation failure (mirrors domain-model ISS-11).

steering_type.description: STEERING: which steering page this rule belongs to (enum-as-string; a new type is a vocabulary bump). OPTIONAL — absent reads back as 'architecture' (the additive default every pre-steering row migrates to on read).

applies_to.description: STEERING inclusion: the phases/tools this rule is selected for (exact token match — the merged Policy.applies_to semantics). OPTIONAL; absent/empty = not phase-scoped.

excludes.description: STEERING exclusion twin of applies_to: a phase token listed here withdraws the rule from that phase even when applies_to includes it — exclusion dominates. OPTIONAL.

weight.description: STEERING ordering weight within a severity band (recall orders severity, then weight DESC, then id) and the stored gate-priority signal. OPTIONAL — absent reads back as 1.0.

effect.description: The merged Policy model's enforcement effect. OPTIONAL: a rule WITHOUT effect is RECALL-ONLY (exactly the v1.0.0 behavior); a rule WITH effect is decide-lane (SELECT/DECIDE fire it; recall does not attach it again).

contains.description: Regex tested over the canonical JSON of the evaluated context (the merged Policy.trigger.contains). Absent (or the whole trigger absent) = fires whenever phase-selected.

trigger.description: The condition under which an effect-bearing rule fires. OPTIONAL.

obligations.description: Obligations collected when a triggered allow_with_conditions effect fires (merged Policy.obligations). OPTIONAL.

criteria.description: Frozen acceptance-criteria text (merged Policy.criteria — becomes the recorded claim's criteria). OPTIONAL.

retired.description: Withdrawn from recall/enforcement (retire-not-delete: the row stays resolvable so past decisions citing it remain explicable). OPTIONAL — absent reads back as active.

schema_version.description: The conformance-rules schema contract version. Every emitted document MUST carry this; a consumer REJECTS a schema_version it has no validator for (no silent best-effort). 1.1.0 adds the OPTIONAL steering fields; 1.0.0 documents validate unchanged. Independent of the @wicked/domain-model-schema bundle semver (VERSION file).

source.description: The repo/service/wiki the rule set was ingested from (optional).

rules.description: The prescriptive rule set. Each item is a pattern or policy Rule. May be empty (a freshly-provisioned, not-yet-ingested store).
